event.name: 17 November 2015 Lefkada, Ionian Sea, Greece, earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Cephalonia Transform Fault Zone, right-lateral strike-slip on the Lefkada segment

reference.title: Slip model of the 17 November 2015 Mw = 6.5 Lefkada earthquake from the joint inversion of geodetic and seismic data

inversion.method: Chousianitis et al. (2016) preferred final joint inversion of static GPS offsets, 1 Hz dynamic GPS, near-field strong-motion accelerograms, and teleseismic P waves. Simulated-annealing kinematic inversion with variable slip, rupture speed, and rise time at each subfault; wavelet-domain seismic misfit, L2 geodetic misfit and space/time regularization. Figure 2 BOTTOM panel (GPS+TELE+SM+1HZGPS), originally 31 x 10 subfaults of 2 x 1.5 km. Reference rupture speed 2.5 km/s, allowable 1.25–3.75 km/s.
inversion.green_function_model: Regional velocity model of Haslinger et al. (1999), adopted for the Ionian Sea; see Chousianitis et al. (2016), section 3.
inversion.notes: FIGURE-RECONSTRUCTED SLIP VALUES, NOT AUTHORS' ORIGINAL NUMERICAL SOLUTION. Figure 2, bottom (preferred GPS+TELE+SM+1HZGPS) panel of Chousianitis et al. (2016), DOI 10.1002/2016GL069764. The original inversion plane is 62 x 15 km, strike N24E, dip 80 degrees, with 31 x 10 original 2 x 1.5 km subfaults. This JSON generates 310 estimates on the published nominal 31 x 10 geometry by regularly sampling the displayed raster panel. The printed vertical color bands do not uniquely establish the boundaries of all 10 downdip model rows: downdip registration is approximate and should NOT be mistaken for the original 310 inversion coefficients. along_strike_km increases SW->NE (from the SW edge of the fault). Down_dip_km is true along-plane distance, while depth_km = down_dip_km * sin(80deg), with assumed upper fault edge at 0-km depth. The figure prints depth, not along-plane dip distance. No numeric array was supplied in the PDF. Image colorbar was digitized from 0–2.5 m and matched to unoccluded cell pixels; black rupture-front contours, white slip-direction arrows, red hypocenter star, axis, and other graphic overlays excluded by palette-distance filtering. Sample estimates are rounded to 0.01 m for data storage, not actual accuracy; see QA CSV for coverage and ambiguity flags. Image-derived colors redder than the publication's stated global maximum of 2.35 m are capped to 2.35 m because the published value is the defensible upper bound, as flagged per-cell in CSV. The published two main asperities southwest of epicenter reach 2.35 m (approx 5 km depth) and a minor northeast deeper patch peaks near 0.7 m; paper reports two main asperities release 65% of moment. SUMMARY max_slip_m=2.35 is REPORTED. SUMMARY mean_slip_m is an image-derived whole-plane arithmetic mean, NOT a published rupture-only mean; the model is approximate. Every patch rake_deg=180 is a nominal right-lateral placeholder, NOT the inverted local vector/rake, which varies in the paper (white arrows). Hypocenter from article: 38.665N,20.600E,depth 11 km, but physical upper fault reference point not tabulated; per-cell latitude,longitude left null. origin_time second precision (07:10:07Z) adopted from the independently digitized Melgar et al. (2017) model of this same event, as the Chousianitis article states 07:10 GMT only. The event_id is for legacy compatibility; current geobrowser matching should group models by event time and location regardless of contributed IDs.

provenance.compiled_by: Figure 2 (last panel) 31x10 source-grid colorbar digitization with per-cell overlay filtering, original paper and user image; observational and publication values distinguished in inversion.notes and accompanying QA
